target_evidence: The exact target asks for either a complete ambiguous visibility-one algorithm for exactly three Batdroids using at most 76 shades, with perpetual exploration under every allowed adversarial execution on every allowed finite grid, or a proof that 77 shades are optimal. The draft establishes neither route: it lacks Cl, Init, a total locally defined T, reachability and boundary handling, adversarial termination, universal perpetual coverage, and any 76-shade impossibility theorem. Its exact-integer coordinate lemmas are nevertheless correct, nonvacuous component results: three finite trace families conditionally establish legal unit/idle movement, exclusivity, and advertised endpoints, while the recurrence establishes frame closure and the boundary examples correctly delimit these statements. They do not establish local implementability or global exploration, so they amount to valid partial progress only. The draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL and its explicit statement that the target remains open are therefore accurate.
